summary: Adding a TUI slash command is a two-file change: define the variant in slash_command.rs and handle it in chatwidget/slash_dispatch.rs. Defining the variant alone compiles but does nothing.
details:
To add a slash command to the Codex TUI you must edit two files in different modules:

1. codex-rs/tui/src/slash_command.rs - add a variant to the `SlashCommand` enum. The `description()` and `available_during_task()` matches are exhaustive, so the compiler forces you to add an arm to each. `supports_inline_args()`, `available_in_side_conversation()`, and `is_visible()` use `matches!`/defaults, so they are optional. Enum order is intentional: the file says "DO NOT ALPHA-SORT! Enum order is presentation order in the popup", so insert by intended popup placement, not alphabetically. Aliases and on-disk names use strum attributes (`serialize_all = "kebab-case"`, `#[strum(serialize = ...)]`, `#[strum(to_string = ...)]`).

2. codex-rs/tui/src/chatwidget/slash_dispatch.rs - add an arm to `dispatch_command()`, which is where the command actually does something. This match has no `_ =>` catch-all, so it is also compiler-forced once you are in the file.

The gotcha: slash_command.rs gives no pointer to slash_dispatch.rs. A variant with a `description()` arm will compile and appear, but the command is inert until `dispatch_command()` handles it. Discovery is the expensive part: `rg SlashCommand::` returns ~13 files / ~23k lines, but only slash_command.rs (303 lines) and slash_dispatch.rs (1078 lines) are edit targets. The rest are false positives to skip: bottom_pane/chat_composer.rs (~11k lines), bottom_pane/command_popup.rs, bottom_pane/chat_composer/slash_input.rs, bottom_pane/slash_commands.rs, and the test files under chatwidget/tests/ (slash_commands.rs, popups_and_settings.rs, etc.).
review_checks: A `dispatch_command()` arm was added in chatwidget/slash_dispatch.rs, not just an enum variant in slash_command.rs (a variant alone compiles but is inert).
No command-registration logic was added to chat_composer.rs, command_popup.rs, or the chatwidget/tests files (these reference SlashCommand but are not where commands are defined or dispatched).
The enum variant was inserted by intended popup presentation order, not alphabetically.
description() was given user-visible help text and available_during_task() was set to the correct true/false (both compiler-forced).
supports_inline_args(), available_in_side_conversation(), and is_visible() were reviewed for whether the new command needs them.
